explanation: The main character in the book of Joshua, who succeeds Moses as leader of the people of Israel.
The land and territories that God has promised to give to the tribes of Israel.
The divine instructions and commandments given by God to Moses on Mount Sinai, including the Ten Commandments.
Bravery and determination in the face of difficulties and challenges; a quality Joshua is encouraged to have.
To reach goals or achieve success, especially when it comes to leading the people of Israel into the promised land.
To move from one place to another, specifically across the Jordan River, which separates the wilderness from the promised land.
A metaphor for presence and control, used to express that wherever Joshua's foot treads, he will gain dominion over it.
